verses.1: Then Zophar the Naamathite responded and said:
verses.2: Therefore my thoughts must be returned to me, and your words must strike me.
verses.3: I will listen to the instruction of my suffering, and the spirit from my understanding will answer me.
verses.4: Have you not known from the beginning, since humanity was placed upon the earth?
verses.5: The joy of the wicked is but a fleeting shadow, and the delight of the arrogant is but a momentary flash.
verses.6: If he ascends to heaven, let him be lifted up, and may his head touch the clouds.
verses.7: Like a wheel he will be driven away, and he will be lost forever. Those who see him will say, "Where is he?"
verses.8: He will fly away like a dream and not be found; he will be chased as a vision in the night.
verses.9: The eye that saw him will no longer see, and the place of his dwelling will no longer look for him.
verses.10: His sons will be scattered to the poor, and his hands will give up their plunder.
verses.11: His bones will be filled with his youthful vigor, and with him he will lie down in the dust.
verses.12: If he delights in evil in his mouth, he will hide it under his tongue,
verses.13: he will not abandon it, nor let it go; he will keep it in the depths of his throat.
verses.14: His bread becomes bitter to his insides; what he longs for is the gall of serpents.
verses.15: He devoured riches, but will vomit them up; what he took into his belly, the god of the gods will give him back.
verses.16: He lapped up riches like a serpent, but the tongue of a viper will slay him.
verses.17: He did not see the rivers of the meadows, the streams of honey and oil.
verses.18: He returned to his house empty, not having taken in; the wages of his toil did not satisfy.
verses.19: For he broke down the houses of the strong, and seized their livelihood, but did not build it up.
verses.20: There is no peace in his stomach, and his delight will not rescue him.
verses.21: No one will deliver him from his possessions; therefore, his good will not endure.
verses.22: When he is full to his fill, his evil will stir; every hardship will come to him.
verses.23: May it be for the one who fills his belly that he sends out wrath upon him, and pours out pain upon him.
verses.24: He will not escape from the hand of iron, the bow of bronze will devour him.
verses.25: The spear will pierce through his body, and terror will walk over his food.
verses.26: All darkness is hidden for his treasures; fire consumes them—unquenched fire, and no survivor remains in his tent.
verses.27: The heavens will reveal his iniquity, and the earth will rise up against him.
verses.28: The harvest of his house will be carried off, in the day of his anger.
verses.29: This is the portion of the wicked man from God, and the heritage of the unjust from the Almighty.

notes:
Notes
- v. 25: "terror will walk over his food" reflects the poetic personification in the Hebrew, where "stars" in the Septuagint (LXX) are likely a misinterpretation of a metaphor.
- v. 27: "the heavens will reveal his iniquity" reflects the Hebrew text's contrast between divine justice and earthly consequences; the LXX's "the heavens will uncover his lawlessness" is similar in meaning.
- v. 29: "the heritage of the unjust from the Almighty" renders "מֵאֵֽל" as "from the Almighty" to match the context of divine judgment, though "El" could also be rendered as "God."
